found: Programs open themselves to agents through MCP, an open standard - creative programs (Blender, Photoshop, GIMP, Aseprite) already do. For terminal programs, MCP servers run them in a pseudo-terminal, send keys, wait on the screen and read it through a terminal model - the descendants of expect (1990); the ones found are Python. Testing tools write scenes with expectations on the screen (tui-test) or turn scripts into recordings (vhs). Rust has the pieces: pseudo-terminals, a terminal emulator as a library, and MCP's official SDK. Graphical programs are reached through AT-SPI or their own connectors.
question: How can an agent use and check interactive tools without a person at the keyboard?

found: Domain-driven design keeps one ubiquitous language used the same way in talk, code and documents - a word with two meanings is a bug. Orwell and the plain-language guidelines ask for the short everyday word a reader already knows, one term for one thing, and no jargon where an everyday word will do. So: look at what others call the thing and what the reader knows, prefer the plain word, keep one meaning, and record the words rejected.
question: How should the commons choose its words?

found: Text patches break on formatting: nineteen times a pattern written for one layout met another. Structural tools (ast-grep on tree-sitter, Comby, rust-analyzer's replace) match code as code. Tried on a real bug: ast-grep matched a whole function by its signature and replaced it; it did not see an expression inside a write! macro, because macro insides are tokens. So: replace whole items, keep logic outside macros, put new views in new files, and let every edit stop the job when it does not take.
question: How should code be changed so an edit cannot silently miss?

found: Site reliability engineering names it toil - manual, repetitive, automatable, without enduring value - and keeps it within a budget. Perceived exertion is rated on one 0-10 scale (Borg CR10); workload can be split into six parts (NASA-TLX), too heavy for every record. Whether automation pays is time per occurrence times frequency (xkcd 1205). Toyota's jidoka makes the machine judge and stop itself, so no person stands by to judge.
question: How do people measure repetitive manual work and how draining it is, and decide when to automate it?
